title: Shared codebook of learned SpinQuant-like layer rotations
hypothesis: A four-entry rotation codebook learned from training layers can match independent per-matrix quantization quality on held-out layers while reducing code bytes and total int4 payload bytes.
physical_object: 12 Pythia-70M attention-output and MLP-up-projection matrices, each input width 512
mirror_coordinate: Per-matrix codebook index selecting an exact block-Hadamard/sign/permutation view
logical_multiplicity: Different quantization coordinate roles across layers; function-preserving full precision

codebook.selection: greedy minimizing mean minimum calibration-row NRMSE across training-layer matrices
codebook.assignment: minimum calibration-row NRMSE within allowed code set

rows.audit_rows: complementary held-out output rows per matrix

development.selection_metric: held-out-layer NRMSE versus independent per-matrix selection; actual total and code-only bytes

paid_objects: packed int4 weights for all 12 matrices
rotation codebook or independent sign/permutation codes

success_gate: Both dev worlds: held-out-layer NRMSE <=1.05x independent per-matrix selection; rotation-code bytes reduced >=50%; full serialized payload reduced >=0.1% versus independent selection.
failure_gate: Any quality or bytes gate miss, or exact native codebook parameter/output alias.
boundaries: Real checkpoint weights but matrix reconstruction only
Fresh codebook seeds stay sealed after a dev gate miss
